reasoning_content:
User 1 has role=2, which is super_admin. This confirms that an admin user was created and seeded.

Next, I'll verify whether login works end-to-end with the documented credentials. I'll check the bin/setup output to see how the admin credentials were generated. Let me actually test the login flow:

1. Get the CSRF token from the sign-in page
2. POST the login

I'll also check whether the bin/setup output is recorded somewhere. I'll check the logs for the bin/setup execution.

action.command: cd /tmp && rm -f cj.txt && TOKEN=$(curl -s -c cj.txt http://localhost:3000/users/sign-in | grep -o 'name="authenticity_token" value="[^"]*"' | head -1 | sed 's/.*value="//;s/"$//'); echo "token len: ${#TOKEN}"; curl -s -b cj.txt -c cj.txt -o /dev/null -w 'POST /users/sign_in -> %{http_code} redirect: %{redirect_url}\n' -X POST http://localhost:3000/users/sign_in --data-urlencode "authenticity_token=$TOKEN" --data-urlencode "user[email]=admin@example.org" --data-urlencode "user[password]=TTOF3UHA0bsQ"; curl -s -b cj.txt -o /dev/null -w 'GET / after login -> %{http_code}\n' http://localhost:3000/; curl -s -b cj.txt http://localhost:3000/api/users/info | head -c 600; echo
